title: Wren and the Border
premise: Dominic Ashgrove, a disgraced private security contractor haunted by a botched extraction that killed a journalist, discovers his own voiceprint was used to unlock a server containing proof that the 'incident' was orchestrated by a transnational security consortium. Hunted by an assassin codenamed Vesper and disavowed by every agency he once served, Dominic crosses three borders with a burned archivist named Wren, the only person who can authenticate the files. As governments close in and allies betray him, Dominic must choose between disappearing forever and testifying to a truth that will destroy him along with the consortium. In the end, he gets the archive out at terrible cost—Wren dies buying him the final hour—and delivers it not to a court, but to the public, finding a fragile belonging among the people he once protected from a distance.
about_author: Sebastian Galloway is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade working border corridors across Eastern Europe and West Africa before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary professionals caught in machinery far larger than themselves.

chapters.title: The Man Who Slept Standing Up
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Working a routine protection detail in Riga, Dominic reveals his insomnia and hypervigilance through ritual: checking exits, counting heartbeats, never sitting with his back to doors. A client mentions a name from his past—the incident—and Dominic's composure cracks for the first time. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A dead client's encrypted server unlocks using Dominic's own voice, sampled without his knowledge years ago. Inside: financial trails linking the consortium to the ambush that killed journalist Mara Osei. He realizes someone wanted him to find this—or wanted him found. Emotional beat: vertigo as his identity becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV (unnamed). Introduced mid-contract, methodical and oddly courteous, reviewing Dominic's file like a biography of a man already dead. We learn the consortium fears the archive more than any government. Emotional beat: cold intimacy; the reader knows the hunter better than the hunted does.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He tracks the server's other access log to Wren Okonkwo, a former archivist living off-grid in Tallinn who authenticated the files. She refuses to help until he admits what really happened during the incident—that he froze. Emotional beat: reluctant recognition between two people hiding from themselves.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Consortium fixer Elena Marsh briefs officials in three capitals, each offered a sanitized version of the archive. Dominic learns via a burner contact that extradition requests are being drafted against him. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; the law itself is the trap.

chapters.title: The Ferry to Helsinki
chapters.summary: Dominic and Wren's POV, alternating. They move by ferry with forged credentials while Vesper boards behind them. A near-encounter in the galley forces them to abandon luggage and identities. First real conversation about trust. Emotional beat: adrenaline laced with unexpected companionship.

chapters.title: What Mara Left Behind
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback chapters within her memory: how she met Mara Osei, why she kept copies of everything, and her guilt at surviving when Mara didn't. She gives Dominic the authentication key but keeps one file back. Emotional beat: grief converted into purpose.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Hiding in a Stockholm safehouse, they calculate odds: three governments, one assassin, forty-eight hours before the archive is legally seized. Dominic sleeps for the first time in months—two hours, dreamless—and wakes ashamed of the relief. Emotional beat: exhaustion and tenderness.

chapters.title: Marsh
chapters.summary: Elena Marsh's POV. The fixer offers Dominic immunity in exchange for the archive and silence, revealing she engineered his voiceprint unlock deliberately—to flush out Wren. Emotional beat: seductive corruption; the offer is genuinely tempting.

chapters.title: The Turncoat
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. His old handler, Ivo Lindqvist, agrees to smuggle them south—but Vesper has already bought him. An ambush at a rail yard kills Ivo; Dominic saves Wren by revealing skills he swore he'd buried. Emotional beat: rage and self-recognition—he is still the weapon he tried to stop being.

chapters.title: Border Country
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On foot through forested borderland, Wren confesses the withheld file: footage showing Dominic didn't freeze—he was ordered to stand down, then scapegoated. Her withholding was fear he'd quit. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into forgiveness.

chapters.title: Vesper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Interrogating a captured courier, we learn Vesper's contract includes a kill clause on everyone involved—including Marsh. The assassin begins keeping a private ledger of the consortium's crimes instead of deleting them. Emotional beat: a conscience waking inside a professional.

chapters.title: Copenhagen Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A planned handoff to a journalist goes wrong; the drop is compromised, the journalist arrested. Dominic realizes only broadcast—not custody—can protect the archive now. Emotional beat: strategy hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Trapped overnight in a cargo terminal, Dominic and Wren keep watch in shifts, trading stories about the people they failed. For the first time, Dominic sleeps deeply beside someone else. Emotional beat: intimacy as sanctuary before the storm.

chapters.title: Seizure
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV. Consortium lawyers obtain emergency seizure orders in two countries simultaneously; the archive will be 'legally' erased within days. Marsh, rattled by Vesper's ledger surfacing, starts covering her own tracks. Emotional beat: the machine beginning to eat itself.

chapters.title: Amsterdam Gambit
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They surface publicly—deliberately—to draw Vesper away from the backup drive Wren cached. Dominic lets himself be captured, betting his interrogation buys Wren time. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In a black-site room, Marsh offers truth for truth: the consortium built the incident to bury Mara's reporting. Dominic records everything on a implant mic, gambling they won't check a broken man. Emotional beat: quiet defiance under pressure.

chapters.title: Vesper's Choice
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Ordered to execute Dominic and close the ledger, Vesper instead releases him with the recording and turns toward the consortium's board. Emotional beat: the assassin choosing justice over contract.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. Wren streams the archive and Dominic's recording across mirrored servers as Vesper holds off consortium enforcers and Marsh tries a last negotiation. Wren takes a fatal shot ensuring the upload completes. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with unbearable loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Governments scramble, arrests begin, and Dominic—technically guilty of many things—is quietly let go because prosecuting him would validate the archive. He attends no hearings. Emotional beat: hollow victory, justice outside the law.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He visits Mara's family and Wren's sister, giving them the unredacted truth and accepting their anger. He stops guarding clients nobody trusts. Emotional beat: accountability as the first honest act.

chapters.title: Border Light
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, epilogue. Months later, teaching security awareness to journalists in a border town, Dominic sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. A postcard arrives, unsigned, from someone who owes him nothing and knows everything. Emotional beat: guarded peace, finally earned.
